December 2009 # **23****rd** **November - 4****th** **December 2009** # **Spot TC/RC market stays quiet** Before the outcome of TC/RC annual negotiations emerges, the spot concentrate market has been very quiet recently. TC/RC quotations have declined to $8/0.8¢ now, compared to $10/0.1¢ a few weeks ago. There are almost no deals happening at this price because many smelters are negotiating their annual contracts and are not buying concentrates in the spot market. Lower spot TC/RCs will surely have an impact on the annual negotiation. It is reported that the Chinese smelters have finished preliminary negotiations and exchanged views of the concentrate market with miners but have not settled their TC/RC. Market insiders within China said that the TC/RC may be settled in the next two weeks during the second round of negotiations. Currently both sides seem to be reluctant to give an estimate on what the TC/RC may be. BHP’s quotation is particularly important. Due to the tight global concentrates market and low spot TC/RCs, the Chinese smelters are at a disadvantage in the negotiations. However, their negotiating stance - striving for a better process fee or accepting an offer passively - will make a big difference to the final outcome. We believe that the domestic suppliers will adopt a positive and active attitude. However, the concentrate market is clearly in a deficit right now, whilst Chinese new and currently expanded smelting capacity is being squeezed between local government pressure to boost local economies and jobs on the one hand and high investment cost, on the other. # **Annual cathode contracts dragging on while spot premium rises** Until now consumers had shown little enthusiasm to commit to annual cathode contracts for 2010 after Codelco’s announcement of the China premium of $85/t. Some consumers actually prefer dealing with Codelco rather than other traders as the $10/t (or larger) price gap is makes an insignificant difference given that the copper price has climbed to over $7,000/t.. © 2009 CRU International Limited **confidential** **December 2009** www.crumonitor.com ## **Premium of imported cathode stabilises** $/t

Nevertheless, most of the consumers are likely to delay their commitment to a contract to the first quarter in 2010. The spot premium for imported copper cathode is now $40-60/t. The premium for imported SXEW cathode is quoted at $40-50/t. Premium quotations have declined but the realised premium is starting to rise due to the narrowing of the negative arbitrage between SHFE and LME and the improved market confidence th

at copper prices will remain well supported. # **Contango moves to backwardation as scrap traders hold back material** The SHFE cash price has climbed above RMB55,000/t while the spot market has switched from contango to backwardation. Usually consumption would be dampened by a high price, especially with the abundant domestic cathode supply in China at the moment. The move to backwardation was mainly attributed to scrap market developments. According to the official custom data, China imported 262,424t of scrap (gross weight) in October, down 36% on September. With the copper price climbing, some scrap traders were reluctant to sell, which consequently led to a decline in the scrap discount. Market insiders believe that scrap supply may tighten again as custom checks remain strict and import deposits have increased. We also understand that scrap traders in Tianjin are building stocks as they wait for the price to rise higher in order to achieve a better profit. **ChineseSHFE inventorycoimports of of imported copperper scrap imports heads higher (000t) concentrate (monthly)(monthly, gross weight)** '000 t

# **Will the copper price maintain an upward trend?** The positive market sentiment, a weaker US dollar and an increase in investment flows have been the main drivers of the copper price, while fundamentals appear to have been forgotten by the market. The LME 3-month copper price jumped to a high of $7,125/t on 3rd December. The Dubai default worry has eased and the US dollar weakened further, so funds appear to have moved back to commodities, driving the copper price to a new record high for 2009. Subsequently, the SHFE 3-month copper price rose to RMB55,680/t while the spot market backwardation moved to RMB50/t. © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 3 **December 2009** www.crumonitor.com As mentioned above, the scrap shortage has caused those consumers that can do so to switch to cathode from scrap. If the scrap shortage does not ease soon, SHFE stocks may decline which in turn would support the copper price to maintain a high level. Also, one should pay attention as the end of the year approaches when some funds may sell copper due to profit-taking. We therefore predict that the copper price may continue to fluctuate around RMB55-56,000/t in the next two weeks and will not be surprised with a new record high given positive economic sentiment.
